overview: Two fundamental research settings, distinguished by whether an experiment happens outside or inside a living organism.
genZNote: In vitro: science in a dish. In vivo: science inside a living thing.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Experiments conducted outside a living organism, typically in a controlled artificial environment such as a test tube, petri dish, or cell culture.
aspects.valueB: Experiments conducted within a living organism, capturing the full complexity of an intact biological system.

aspects.label: Environment
aspects.valueA: Isolated, artificial, and highly controlled (e.g. cell lines, purified proteins, cultured tissue).
aspects.valueB: The full, complex physiological environment of a living organism (e.g. animal models, clinical trials).

aspects.label: Control and Simplicity
aspects.valueA: Easier to control variables and isolate specific mechanisms, but may not reflect whole-organism behavior.
aspects.valueB: More biologically realistic, but more variables and complexity make it harder to isolate a single mechanism.

aspects.label: Ethical and Cost Considerations
aspects.valueA: Generally lower cost and fewer ethical concerns.
aspects.valueB: Higher cost, longer timelines, and greater ethical oversight (especially for animal or human studies).

aspects.label: Typical Use in Drug Development
aspects.valueA: Early-stage screening of drug candidates, mechanism studies.
aspects.valueB: Later-stage testing of efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics in a whole living system before/during clinical use.
